title: JC H2 physics — thermal: kinetic theory, gas laws and temperature
subject: science

scenes.caption: Temperature: molecules jiggle faster when hotter

shape.explain: A sealed box of gas — the same molecules in every beat.
A gas molecule — its jitter is its kinetic energy.
Another molecule — hotter means harder jitter, for all of them.
A third molecule — watch its jitter grow as the dial turns.
A fourth molecule — same gas, same rising temperature.
Temperature dial — the needle turns up as the gas heats.
Dial needle — watch it turn through the three beats.
300 K: the coolest case, slowest jiggle.
450 K: warmer, faster jiggle.
600 K: the hottest case, fastest jiggle.

steps.text: Hotter: the same molecules jiggle faster

scenes.narration: Temperature is the average kinetic energy of the molecules. Turn the dial from 300 to 600 kelvin and the same four molecules jiggle harder and faster — nothing else changes. That is what hotter means.

scenes.caption: Conduction: heat travels atom by atom

shape.explain: A metal rod — energy enters at the hot end and hops atom to atom.
A metal lattice atom — it passes the jiggle to its neighbour.
A metal lattice atom — it passes the jiggle to its neighbour.
A metal lattice atom — it passes the jiggle to its neighbour.
A metal lattice atom — it passes the jiggle to its neighbour.
A metal lattice atom — it passes the jiggle to its neighbour.
The hot end — energy packets start here.
An energy packet — watch it hop atom to atom down the rod.
The far end of the rod warms — the jiggle has arrived.

steps.text: Heat conducts as atoms pass the jiggle along

scenes.narration: Hold one end of a metal rod to a flame and the hot atoms jiggle hard, bumping their neighbours, which bump theirs. The jiggle travels as heat, atom by atom, until the far end warms up.

scenes.caption: Convection: the fluid loops

shape.explain: A tank of fluid — warm fluid rises on one side, cool fluid sinks on the other.
The heater — it warms the fluid touching it, which expands and rises.
A warmed parcel — hot fluid is less dense, so it rises.
A cooled parcel — cool fluid is denser, so it sinks.
Another rising parcel — the loop keeps turning.

steps.text: Convection: warm rises, cool sinks, the loop turns

scenes.narration: Warm the fluid at the bottom and it expands, grows less dense, and rises. Cool fluid at the top is denser and sinks. Rising on the warm side, sinking on the cool side — the fluid loops itself around.

scenes.caption: Radiation: hotter means more packets, faster

shape.explain: A hot filament — it radiates energy packets in every direction.
300 K radiation: fewer, slower packets.
Radiated power — the bar grows as the body heats: hotter means brighter.
A radiated packet — energy leaving the hot body.
600 K radiation: more, faster packets.
More packets at 600 K — intensity rises with temperature.
A third packet — hotter bodies radiate more, and faster.
Stefan-Boltzmann law — radiated power grows as the fourth power of temperature.
A cooler body — it still radiates, but far fewer packets, and slower.
One slow packet from the cool body — every body radiates something.

steps.text: Hotter bodies radiate more packets, and faster

scenes.narration: Every hot body radiates energy as packets flying outward. Heat the filament from 300 to 600 kelvin and the packets come faster and thicker — the power bar climbs as the fourth power of temperature, the Stefan-Boltzmann law. Even the cool body radiates: one slow packet, still on its way.

scenes.caption: Misconception: a common mistake about heat and temperature

shape.explain: A small cup of hot water — high temperature, little water.
A big bucket of warm water — lower temperature, far more water.
The 80 C bucket: hotter, but holds less heat.
The 30 C tub: cooler, but holds far more heat.

shape.text: Temperature measures how much heat a body holds
shape.explain: The wrong idea — temperature is the average, not the total.
Total heat in the cup — the bar grows with the total energy.
Total heat in the bucket — far more water, far more total energy.

shape.text: Heat is the total; temperature is the average
shape.explain: The fix: heat adds up every molecule; temperature averages them.

steps.text: Misconception: a common mistake about heat and temperature

scenes.narration: A common mistake: thinking temperature measures how much heat a body holds. Heat is the total kinetic energy — every molecule's share added up. Temperature is the average per molecule. The small hot cup has the higher temperature; the big warm bucket holds far more heat.
